chunks: Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ṣabbāḥ al-Azraq, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) عليهما السلام, who said:

Indeed, among the most severe circumstances for the people on the Day of qiyamah is that the صاحبُ الْخُمُسِ should stand and say: “O my Lord, my khums.” And we have made that lawful for our Shi'ah so that their births may be wholesome and their births may be purified.

key_terms.الْخُمُسِ: khums, the one-fifth due designated as a financial right
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shi'ah, the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.صَاحِبُ الْخُمُسِ: the one entitled to the right of khums
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Resurrection and final reckoning

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about khums and the condition of people on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a severe scene of reckoning on the Day of qiyamah related to the right of khums. It states that the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام made this matter lawful for their Shi'ah so that their lineage and birth would remain pure and wholesome.
